subject: Transportation Systems
title: High-Speed Changes Everything
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on High-Speed Changes Everything.

hook.text: Japan's Shinkansen launched in 1964. Tokyo to Osaka dropped from seven hours to four.

buildup.text: High-speed rail thrives between 100 and 500 miles—too far to drive, too short to fly.

discovery.text: In that sweet spot, trains beat planes once you add check-in, security, and the taxi to the airport.

twist.text: Building it is expensive. California budgeted $33 billion for high-speed rail. The cost tripled.

climax.text: Where it works—Japan, France, China—high-speed rail reshapes how cities connect.

quiz.question: In what distance range does high-speed rail beat air travel?
